Looking one last time at our work on DiscourseGraphs accounts.  https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/H3a0tja8D 
One thing that I think is missing: What are the UX touchpoints. We have to make people of whether and how they are logged in on each platform, and sometimes in non-obvious places like if they're doing a non-local search, for example. I may be worth enumerating this.

11	Exploration of personal accounts (Linear project "Discourse Graph Accounts", Roam project page Tow9ZlFAi). The working document is Roam page "Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts" (H3a0tja8D). I write there directly, and only there. It maps options with costs for the group; the user does not want premature decisions, and decisions in older notes are not settled.
12	
13	Decided or strong leanings, as of 2026-10-23:
14	- Cross-space search inside the platforms; `Website` joins the `Platform` enum; password accounts stay; no forcing Roam users to sign up; Roam API tokens need a subscription, so token-based proof is never required.
15	- A person reaches a space only through a claimed PlatformAccount (A, B and any direct person-to-space edge ruled out). Preferred: claim reach scoped by attestation (`asserted` reaches only the vouching space).
16	- No group nesting or recursive queries; no database-level invites into spaces; close the `group_membership` insert hole first.
17	- Space admin = flag plus level on `LocalAccess`: guessed < registered < proven, each with a delegated level just below it; delegates can name same-level delegates; demotion only of strictly lower levels, manual, through an admin UI; the delegator is not recorded. Admins approving identity claims is set aside.
18	- Admin can prove with a backend token, discarded or stored (stored is an explicit opt-in, and enables L6 for the whole graph).
19	- Emails stored but hidden until shared; names are shown as name plus PlatformAccount id. Profile visibility: one row per person and audience with an array of fields.
20	- Two sessions in the plugin: personal for reads, search and actions as the person; space for sync, groups and sharing. Personal session delivery: Supabase Auth as OAuth 2.1 server (plugin is a PKCE client; login always on the Website; MAU cost accepted; completing inside the plugin is nice to have, with a `secret_token` fallback). Social login is for adding identities and logging in on the Website. A claimed account shows the profile name.
21	
22	- Access resolution: three nested sets `self_to_spaces()` (group membership/admin checks), `self_to_groups()` (sharing checks), `self_to_everyone()` (reads), replacing `my_user_accounts()` and ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()`. A person acting for S is admin of G when S is (stage 1); stage 2 restricts that to admins of S. Sets return a cap per uid; the initplan RLS rewrite is a prerequisite.
23	
24	Verified 2026-10-24: Roam clients can't forge `:create/user` (no `roamDatomicAlphaAPI`); only graph owners/admins create backend tokens; Obsidian account ids are per vault (vault name + random suffix, synced with the vault); ORCID can be a Supabase custom OIDC provider (identity linking and `email_optional` still to check); ATProto likely needs its own flow (untested).
25	
26	New layer L8: Roam's Firebase ID token (IndexedDB `firebaseLocalStorageDb`, issuer `securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`, `sub` = Roam uid, verified email) can be checked server-side. Works in the desktop app and in browsers. Blocked until Roam's ToS is checked and Roam agrees.
27	
28	Open: identity-link package (L0–L8, the group's call); Roam token storage pending (memory and a click per reload vs refresh token in `localStorage`); lease length; whether the backend API returns `:user/email`; whether imports keep creator and timestamps; whether the OAuth flow completes inside the plugins. Latent bug: `upsert_account_in_space` copies `SpaceAccess` once `dg_account` is set. ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()` should be renamed `self_to_groups()` before it merges.
29	
30	Answered 2026-10-26: `roamAlphaAPI.user.isAdmin` (synchronous, no parameters, current user only; docs say "admin of this graph (the graph owner)", so whether non-owner admins count is unclear). Recorded under Space admin → Guessed (block SdqDeXOxt): it makes the Roam guess correct but no harder to forge, since it is sent under the space session.
31	
32	Status 2026-10-24: the user marked the page pre-spec (pending decisions) and closed the session.
33	
34	**How to apply:** read the Roam page before resuming; keep mapping, not deciding. Related: [[explain-reasoning-before-options]], [[roam-propose-write-quirks]], [[leaving-group-unpublishes]].

# Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="8"/>

- [[>]] [[!NOTE]] Working document: options and their costs, not decisions <roam uid="S4dKzvDG9"/>
  - This page maps the options for adding personal accounts to Discourse Graphs, so the group can choose. Only the items under "Constraints so far" are settled. Part of [[Project/Discourse Graph Accounts]]. <roam uid="WOKj5fQ9w"/>
  - This was written with OpenSpec, but because there are many pending decisions, we decided to stay at a pre-spec level. <roam uid="gZPUzWdTF" refs="1"/>
- Goal <roam uid="Czog3Tth-"/>
  - A person gets one Discourse Graphs account (a row in `auth.users`) and links to it the platform accounts (`PlatformAccount`) they use in many spaces. <roam uid="c9N0WS5t9"/>
  - That account gives the person every access their spaces have, including access through the groups those spaces belong to. <roam uid="CKv64nUN3"/>
  - The person can link external identities (Google, ORCID, GitHub, ATProto) for login and for visible attribution on published nodes. <roam uid="QJQPmZBiP"/>
  - The person controls how much personal information each audience sees: the public, each group, peers in shared spaces. <roam uid="vzf6T7khx"/>
  - Account management lives on the Website. Accounts are usually created from a platform, but creating one on the Website is also possible. <roam uid="21Ug7tPlh"/>
  - A visitor who reads published content on the Website has an easy path to an account, so they can propose a connected node. <roam uid="qw2XRjp6E"/>
- Constraints so far <roam uid="1Jt5g8iXN"/>
  - Cross-space search must work inside the platforms, not only on the Website. <roam uid="0vB3AfOoR" refs="1"/>
  - `Website` will be added to the `Platform` enum. <roam uid="EZt61u4zE"/>
  - Accounts with passwords stay available. OAuth is an option for cheap re-login, not a requirement. <roam uid="7dKq3Yhma"/>
  - Roam users must not be forced to create a Discourse Graphs account to keep using the plugin. <roam uid="0_gumN62h"/>
  - A Roam graph token held by our server is not planned for other reasons. It stays open as a security option. <roam uid="TSkb7P3am"/>
  - Groups don't contain groups. Access resolution may add one join, but never a recursive query. <roam uid="spmrIYz0n"/>
  - The hole in the `group_membership` insert policy (anyone can join a uid that has no members yet) is closed before any of this work. <roam uid="T_bGruFoR"/>
  - No invitation into a space at the database level. Access comes from the two existing mechanisms: an invitation into the platform, or a group created for sharing. <roam uid="67S6n7Vcu"/>
  - A person reaches a space only through a `PlatformAccount` they have claimed. There is no direct edge from a person to a space. <roam uid="I86s3K6ew"/>
- Current state <roam uid="wV0qa8Lj7"/>
  - Today `auth.users` holds only non-person principals. <roam uid="v4T3sJ7nT"/>
    - One pseudo-user per space, with a shared space password stored in the platform settings. Every graph member can read that password. <roam uid="kb_Gd_svI"/>
    - One pseudo-user per group. <roam uid="IH0tyDi5Z"/>
    - The `everyone` pseudo-user for public content (ENG-1837 branch, not merged). <roam uid="oJCpZSrsO"/>
    - Agent users for read-only agent access (planned in the `agent-read-only-access` OpenSpec change). <roam uid="viJKLrjcB"/>
  - A person exists only as a `PlatformAccount` row inside spaces, with `dg_account` empty. <roam uid="IYCyffXJS"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account` already references `auth.users`. Today only the space pseudo-account sets it. <roam uid="f6tgGk3-t"/>
    - `upsert_account_in_space` already writes a `SpaceAccess` row for an account whose `dg_account` is set. This anticipates personal accounts with copied grants. <roam uid="umtrUcTmK"/>
  - The plugins always act as the space. The Website login (`auth/token` route) also hands over the space session, so spaces, not people, create and administer groups. <roam uid="22z7vxaew"/>
  - `my_user_accounts()` is one level deep: the caller plus the groups the caller belongs to. <roam uid="E5xoEdRTK"/>
    - ENG-1837 adds `everyone` to it. The agent change adds the agent's principal and that principal's groups. Personal accounts would be the third change to this function. <roam uid="bUiWiBwvl"/>
  - A Roam user uid is the same in every graph, and `PlatformAccount` is unique on `(account_local_id, platform)`. An Obsidian account looks local to its vault (not verified). <roam uid="0hZ8_lin2"/>
- What personal accounts unblock <roam uid="xf04Pfzph"/>
  - Cross-space search across every space the person can read, without an ad-hoc group. <roam uid="h-4gnZEFx"/>
  - Access through the groups of the person's spaces. <roam uid="VUcgEAHwK"/>
  - Login on the Website without going through a platform. <roam uid="K5GaPtL-U"/>
  - People, not spaces, as group admins. This is where a server-side admin guard (deferred in ENG-1834) belongs. <roam uid="ZaIztzKBk"/>
  - Agent grants owned by a person: an agent reads what its person can read. <roam uid="ZMQawpPb-"/>
  - Visible attribution on published nodes, including ORCID or `did:plc` in the JSON-LD export (`prov:wasAttributedTo`). <roam uid="KFl8nD8ZJ"/>
  - One author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website. <roam uid="1_RnxGUvX"/>
  - Website-native contribution: a personal space on the `Website` platform holds proposed nodes, which connect to published nodes through cross-space relations (ENG-2334 to ENG-2340). <roam uid="mkRPW2jG7"/>
  - Sharing by a person rather than by a space (the open reciprocal-sharing question on the project page). <roam uid="fSlDNn-H-"/>
- Decision: how a personal account is linked to a platform identity <roam uid="HrW3SuczV"/>
  - **Why it matters:** anyone who holds a space password can claim to be any member of that space. This decision sets how much proof a link needs, and therefore whether a co-member can take over another member's attribution and their access to other spaces. Stronger proof costs the person effort or depends on Roam. <roam uid="G_ksAI6Q_"/>
  - The threat <roam uid="6q9kdzcJl"/>
    - Anyone with the space password can mint a claim as that space. In Roam, that is every graph member. <roam uid="3TQldEoEj"/>
    - A co-member can therefore claim another member's Roam uid and take over their attribution, and their access to other spaces if the claim spreads beyond the space. <roam uid="8miESmtZh"/>
    - Outsiders can't do this under any option below. <roam uid="EJZYtvlMR"/>
    - Example: Mallory reads graph A's space password, calls `create_secret_token` as the space with Alice's uid in the payload, opens the link, and logs in with her own Google account. `create_secret_token` accepts any payload from any authenticated caller. <roam uid="6gK3VqcE-"/>
  - Two kinds of claim <roam uid="_oWUtNrtr"/>
    - An access claim is an `asserted` claim: "I am this platform account", vouched for only by one space's session. If it gives access only in that space, a forger gains nothing they don't already have. <roam uid="qbzJP8qlz"/>
    - An identity claim says "this platform account is me". It carries attribution and may spread to other spaces, so it needs stronger proof. <roam uid="jriBBo825"/>
    - The group wants identity, not only access. <roam uid="tre8QheiL"/>
  - Verified identifiers are separate from links <roam uid="o_xM2FmbI"/>
    - A personal account can hold verified identifiers that aren't tied to any platform account: emails, Google or GitHub identities, an ORCID iD, an ATProto handle. <roam uid="rvWITqil4"/>
    - They serve login, the profile, and attribution on their own. <roam uid="cMWL7UAPb"/>
    - An identifier becomes evidence for a link only when a platform records the same identifier for a platform account. That is what L1 checks for email. <roam uid="Q1mfw83z-"/>
    - Obsidian attribution relies on these identifiers, since Obsidian rarely records anything we can check. <roam uid="dPJOYzQfI"/>
  - Email as the bridge <roam uid="WbpaSzu1V"/>
    - The Roam plugin can read `:user/email` through datalog. <roam uid="q37Xq8DVO"/>
    - If the personal account proves control of an email (Google login, or a verification mail) and Roam records that email for the uid, a forger fails: they can't log in as the victim's email. <roam uid="Zt5yx9RoU"/>
    - The weak point is the source of the uid-to-email binding. If it comes from the claim's own payload, the forger writes their own email. Stored `AgentIdentifier` rows can also be poisoned, because RLS lets space editors write identifiers of unclaimed accounts. <roam uid="Qr1nAWi-I"/>
  - Layers <roam uid="tZGbhisXM"/>
    - **Why it matters:** the layers are the choices for the identity-link decision. Each one stops a different kind of forgery, at a different cost to the person and to us. The packages below combine them, so read those first if you only want the trade-offs. <roam uid="jY7-WynXq"/>
    - The layers stack. Each one is described by what it stops and what it costs. <roam uid="fBoQ0vuf5"/>
    - L0: Token handoff only. The plugin mints a `secret_token` with the uid; the person logs in on the Website. <roam uid="_qMYaUHJ0"/>
      - Stops outsiders only. <roam uid="ZjIn7a1og"/>
      - Burden: none. Cost: lowest, reuses the `auth/token` route. Platforms: all. <roam uid="bM5E9fXbZ"/>
    - L1: Email binding. The personal account must control the email that the platform records for the platform account. <roam uid="ShFzQ-cQE"/>
      - Control of the email can be proven two ways, both at this layer: a verification mail, or a linked external identity (Google, GitHub, ...) whose provider vouches that the email is verified. Many Roam users sign in to Roam with Google, so the same Google account often proves the match in one step. <roam uid="0ngOboLPC"/>
      - Only provider emails marked as verified count. Supabase also links identities that share a verified email automatically, so the account's set of verified emails must be read from the account, not from one login. <roam uid="L3hwsR2X1"/>
      - Stops a forger who can't also falsify the binding source. <roam uid="eNir7ER3F"/>
      - Burden: the person verifies once. Cost: low. The verification can start from any plugin or from the Website. Platforms: any platform that records an email for the account. Roam does; for Obsidian, see below. <roam uid="KgXX_YwXm"/>
      - Obsidian <roam uid="cx9aeX2_F"/>
        - The Obsidian plugin sends no email today (`email: undefined` in `supabaseContext.ts`). Whether it can read the email of the Obsidian account, and whether that email is verified, is not checked yet. Using an Obsidian account is optional, so some users have none. <roam uid="sx3sITsvn"/>
        - The binding would come from the plugin, as it does in Roam. But an Obsidian vault rarely has co-members who could forge it, so L1 adds less there. <roam uid="AM08ShSzs"/>
        - An email the person types in is not a platform record. Verifying it gives the personal account a verified identifier, but says nothing about which platform account is theirs. <roam uid="nvfy6pgBo"/>
        - A vault synced between people shares one `PlatformAccount`, so a claim by one of them covers the others' content too. <roam uid="vBcLpeOcv"/>
    - L2: Corroboration. Accept the binding only if two or more spaces recorded it before the claim. <roam uid="sZ85qtOYg"/>
      - Stops a forger who is in only one of the victim's graphs. <roam uid="SK6ZmyFfB"/>
      - Burden: none, but people in a single graph never reach this level. Cost: low, a query over existing rows. <roam uid="-I0HJIpta"/>
    - L3: Conflict detection and notification. Freeze a uid when a competing claim arrives; mail the verified address when a link is made. <roam uid="IjOxjCi1x"/>
      - Prevents nothing, but a forgery is noticed fast and can be reversed. <roam uid="QBboyIbUv"/>
      - Burden: the victim reacts to a notice; someone settles frozen links. Cost: low to medium. Platforms: all. <roam uid="R0WJRywXw"/>
      - Variant: the victim's plugin checks on load <roam uid="_lAmRuC9k"/>
        - The plugin knows the current Roam uid from its own client. On load it asks whether that `PlatformAccount` is claimed. If it is claimed and the person has no personal session, or a different one, the plugin asks "Your Roam identity is linked to a Discourse Graphs account. Was this you?" <roam uid="FNfpjab1n"/>
        - Catches a forgery without email, even when the forger controls the email binding. The damage window lasts until the victim next opens the plugin. <roam uid="ovhYlp3bV"/>
        - Needs a new `SECURITY DEFINER` function that returns only the claim status, not the claimant. `my_accounts` no longer exposes `dg_account`. <roam uid="HU4VT8div"/>
        - Under the space session the caller only asserts their uid, so any member can ask about any co-member ("has X connected a Discourse Graphs account?"). With L8, the plugin can present the Firebase token and the function answers only for the proven uid. <roam uid="NxNh0_jLj"/>
        - Responding can't rest on a bare assertion: if anyone could freeze a claim, a forger could freeze every legitimate claim in the graph. A contest must either bring a proof stronger than the existing claim's attestation (L1, L8), or only notify and flag for review. <roam uid="03ZvE1H1-"/>
    - L4: Per-device keys, trusted on first use. The plugin silently registers a key per browser and Roam user; identity claims must be signed by a registered key. <roam uid="OlDRHI2bI"/>
      - Stops forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run. A key added later for the same uid shows up on the older device as "a new device was registered as you". <roam uid="oZz6BVWjI"/>
      - Burden: users confirm new devices. Cost: medium. Platforms: Roam and Obsidian. <roam uid="_Dcxp_ILa"/>
      - Works without a personal account, so it protects people who never sign up. <roam uid="qKkvxmlvM"/>
      - Caveat: in Roam, every extension shares the roamresearch.com origin. Another extension can use the key while the page is open, but can't export it. <roam uid="HNbfUd67I"/>
    - L5: Admin approval. The space admin confirms identity claims in that space. Set aside: having admins approve someone's identity feels wrong in general. <roam uid="xp07QYFwB"/>
      - Stops forgery by anyone except the admin. <roam uid="H5d_3BrMU"/>
      - Burden: admins, once per claim. Cost: medium, needs the admin role first. Only as strong as the admin proof. <roam uid="hlhlB4Hzw"/>
    - L6: Roam backend attestation. Our server reads the uid-to-email binding from Roam with a graph token. <roam uid="xZ9ZW0mBc"/>
      - Stops all forgery. <roam uid="XbTu0uESn"/>
      - Needs an active Roam subscription to create a backend token. L6 can therefore only be an optional upgrade, never a requirement. <roam uid="aUGQqVVU0"/>
      - A Roam uid is global, so a one-time token from any graph the person owns is enough. No shared-graph admin is needed. <roam uid="-ubL7d6ZM"/>
      - Burden: the person supplies a token once (or an admin stores one). Cost: medium one-time, high if stored (secrets, rotation). Platforms: Roam only. <roam uid="csHZObWSP"/>
      - Variant: a token stored per graph, supplied by an admin. <roam uid="j0wLV46uO"/>
        - Our server can then attest the uid-to-email binding of any member of that graph. Members don't need their own Roam subscription, so L6 becomes available to everyone in that graph. <roam uid="xyNjRWm5g"/>
        - The same token can first attest the admin who supplies it, so their proven admin flag lands on the right `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="IskrgBXJ4"/>
        - Cost: a read-only graph token exposes the whole graph, which is far more than Discourse Graphs stores. It needs encrypted storage readable only by a server-side function (for example Supabase Vault), never by clients. The admin can revoke it in Roam at any time, and then the graph falls back to the weaker layers. <roam uid="WxoAJVdJR"/>
    - L7: Tiered space password. Members get a reader credential; admins hold the editor credential. <roam uid="ipLQprIac"/>
      - Stops forgery by non-admins. <roam uid="TD5X_nVgo"/>
      - Burden: admins distribute and rotate credentials. Cost: medium, and it changes who can sync. <roam uid="dE_FI2cS_"/>
    - L8: Roam sign-in token (candidate). The plugin reads the signed-in user's Firebase ID token from the page and sends it to our server, which checks it and discards it. <roam uid="J0BDirkni"/>
      - Roam uses Firebase Auth. Its ID token is a JWT signed by Google, with issuer `https://securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`. Its claims include the Roam uid (`sub`), the user's email, and `email_verified` (true in the test). The token expires after about an hour. Checked in the Roam desktop app on 2026-10-24. <roam uid="6BQcIhrfL"/>
      - Our server can check the signature against Google's public keys and the audience `firescript-577a2`, without any Roam token. A co-member can't produce another user's token without running code in that user's browser. <roam uid="V1kVD6tTP"/>
      - Stops all forgery, like L6, and works for every Roam user, with no subscription and no admin. <roam uid="zLeqJYcuA"/>
      - Burden: none for the person. Cost: low to medium, one server-side check. <roam uid="QJauyMm3T"/>
      - Caveats <roam uid="Mg5o9FT2O"/>
        - **Blocking: L8 can't be used until we have checked that it doesn't violate Roam's Terms of Service, and Roam has agreed.** Reading another product's session token and sending it to our server may breach those terms even if we only verify it and discard it. <roam uid="on38t4VGv"/>
        - It depends on Roam's internals: the token sits in IndexedDB (`firebaseLocalStorageDb`), which Roam can change without notice. <roam uid="e0BzqzHvE"/>
        - The token also authenticates to Roam itself for about an hour. Our server would briefly hold a credential that can act as the user in Roam. <roam uid="k0stwVkUB"/>
        - Only the short-lived ID token may leave the browser, never the refresh token. <roam uid="Q_jKLTAGF"/>
      - Also checked in a browser on 2026-10-24, in a normal and a private window: the same storage holds the same kind of token. The browser has one auth entry where the desktop app has two (the app adds a `-tx-writer` entry), so the plugin should read the `[DEFAULT]` entry. <roam uid="tRm3RsaGT"/>
  - Packages to compare <roam uid="N3CzNT6ji"/>
    - Minimal: L0 + L1 + L3. Co-member forgery is detected after the fact. Almost no burden. <roam uid="3nc-Wa1fB"/>
    - Medium: Minimal + L2 + L4. Co-member forgery is prevented, except before the victim's first plugin use. Burden: new-device prompts. <roam uid="lpEuCPPEP"/>
    - Strong: Medium + L6 with a one-time token, for people who have a Roam subscription. Forgery is prevented for them. Burden: one token per person, once. Everyone else stays at Medium. <roam uid="ES2_RxYVo"/>
    - Admin-centric: L0 + L5 + L3. Set aside with L5. <roam uid="zo5JtOuJ8"/>
    - Because L6 is optional, Medium is the strongest level every user can reach. In it, L4 does most of the work against co-member forgery. <roam uid="GELnQvnLI"/>
    - Strong for everyone, if L8 is allowed: Medium + L8. Forgery is prevented for every Roam user, with no token and no subscription. Depends on Roam's agreement and on its internals staying stable. <roam uid="tsWkLqVnK"/>
  - Applies to every option <roam uid="inXsU_Qm3"/>
    - Record an attestation level on each link (`asserted`, `corroborated`, `attested`) and let policies read the level, never the platform. This lets us start low and add layers without migrating policies. <roam uid="UfKqf9ASZ"/>
    - Example policy: export `prov:wasAttributedTo` only for `attested` links. <roam uid="w7SPEavvQ"/>
    - Platform-specific verification is expected. Multi-user platforms (Roam) have a server that can attest identity; local single-user platforms (Obsidian) have no co-member to forge against. <roam uid="mk9A0_wN6"/>
    - Obsidian links stay `asserted` in every option. Obsidian attribution comes from the person's verified identifiers, not from the platform account. <roam uid="eGU1Y7Vyj"/>
- Decision: how a person gets a space's access <roam uid="4Rqcs56zH"/>
  - **Why it matters:** this sets which spaces a personal account can read and act for. The open question, how far a weakly proven claim reaches, decides whether cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="NQeAiZ8V4"/>
  - Ruled out <roam uid="1FYnwOB2T"/>
    - A: copy `SpaceAccess` and group rows to the person. The copies outlive the relation they came from. <roam uid="BGRs-LBmc"/>
    - Any edge from a person to a space that skips the `PlatformAccount`. This rules out B (the person as a member of the space pseudo-user in `group_membership`) and a separate person-to-space table. <roam uid="FKZQENpx6"/>
      - The `PlatformAccount` is where a person exists inside a space. Authorship, `LocalAccess` and identifiers hang off it. <roam uid="Z4r63tySQ"/>
      - A second track could disagree with it: a person could have a space's access through one edge while their `PlatformAccount` in that space is unclaimed, or claimed by someone else. <roam uid="2xyckcERL"/>
  - Model: claims through a PlatformAccount <roam uid="j2yrxCKys"/>
    - A claim links a personal account to a `PlatformAccount`. The person then acts for spaces where that `PlatformAccount` has a `LocalAccess` row. <roam uid="GMJo8AmA_"/>
    - `my_user_accounts()` adds those spaces' pseudo-users and the spaces' groups. The depth is fixed: one extra join, no recursion. <roam uid="5xZCf-gL6"/>
    - A person can also be a direct member of real groups, for example as a group admin. <roam uid="BobollM8N"/>
  - Open: how far a claim reaches <roam uid="5XbPKQsOm"/>
    - Option 1: reach follows identity. <roam uid="tYOGxPCv6"/>
      - Every claim is an identity claim. Access covers every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="KS_8ViwDE"/>
      - Access needs identity proof first, so cross-space search waits on the identity-link decision. <roam uid="K210qCY9T"/>

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

- UX touchpoints: where a person must see how they are logged in
  - **Why it matters:** a plugin holds a space session and maybe a personal session, and a personal claim can be asserted, attested, frozen or expired. The same action gives different results in each state, often silently: RLS returns an empty list, not an error. Every surface below has to tell the person which state applies, or they will read "no access" as "nothing there". Each touchpoint is UI work, so this list is also a cost.
  - States the UI has to distinguish
    - No personal account. This is the default for most Roam users, and it stays a supported state.
    - Personal account, but this platform account isn't claimed.
    - Claimed, `asserted`: the claim reaches only the vouching space.
    - Claimed, `corroborated` or `attested`: the claim reaches every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`.
    - Claim frozen by conflict detection (L3).
    - Claimed by a different personal account than the one signed in on this device.
    - Personal session lost: page reload with memory-only storage, refresh token revoked, or lease expired.
    - Admin level in this space (guessed, registered, proven, each with a delegated level), and whether the claim is strong enough to use it.
  - Plugins (Roam and Obsidian)
    - Status indicator: always visible, shows the space session and the personal session, the account name, and the claim level. Roam: settings panel and maybe a topbar icon. Obsidian: status bar and settings tab.
    - First run: offers to connect a personal account, and says plainly that skipping it loses nothing the plugin does today.
    - Connect and reconnect: the button that opens the Website popup (OAuth with PKCE), or the browser tab of the `secret_token` fallback. In Roam with memory-only storage, a "Reconnect" prompt after each reload.
    - OAuth consent screen on the Website: names the plugin and the space that asks to act as the person.
    - Cross-space search
      - Without a personal session, results cover this space and its groups only. The search UI says so and offers to sign in.
      - With `asserted` claims, results cover only the spaces the person connected one by one. The UI lists the spaces searched, and says how to add others (open the plugin there, or prove identity).
      - A space whose lease expired drops out of results without notice unless the UI lists it.
      - Each result shows its source space, so the person knows where an import would come from.
    - Import from another space (cross-space relations, "DG: Discover shared nodes"): the read runs as the person, the write lands in the local graph. If the personal session drops mid-import, the person sees which part didn't complete.
    - Publishing and sharing to groups: runs as the space. The UI says "this space shares with group G", not "you share", and lists the groups the space belongs to.
    - Accepting a group invitation: the space joins, not the person. The prompt says so. If joining becomes an admin power, the prompt also says who can accept.
    - Admin actions (rotate the space password, join or leave groups, demote, delegate, supply a backend token): shows the person's admin level, and why an action is unavailable (for example "your claim is only asserted").
    - Claim check on load (L3 variant): "Your Roam identity is linked to a Discourse Graphs account. Was this you?" It must tell apart "you, signed out" from "someone else", or legitimate users learn to dismiss it.
    - New-device notice (L4): "a new device was registered as you" on the older device, and a confirmation on the new one.
    - Authorship display: other people appear as profile name, or as name plus `PlatformAccount` id, depending on their claim and on which audiences the viewer belongs to. Two viewers can see different names for the same author.
    - Own attribution: if attribution export requires `attested`, the person sees that their published nodes carry no `prov:wasAttributedTo`, and how to raise the claim level.
  - Website
    - Signed-in banner: "signed in as Alice" or "viewing as space S". Today the `auth/token` route hands over the space session, so both kinds of login exist.
    - Login page: password, social login, ORCID.
    - Account page: claimed platform accounts with their level and vouching space; the spaces this account reaches; verified identifiers; devices and plugin sessions, with a way to revoke them.
    - Profile visibility: a preview of what each audience (public, group, shared-space peers) sees.
    - Visitor reading published content: sees public content only, and a prompt to sign in or create an account to see more or propose a connected node.
  - Outside the apps
    - Verification mail for email binding (L1), started from a plugin or the Website.
    - Link notification mail (L3): "your Roam account was linked to a Discourse Graphs account".
    - Agents: an agent owned by a person reads what that person reads. The grant screen shows the person's current reach, which changes as claims and leases change.
  - Edge cases that change what a touchpoint shows
    - Several Roam graphs open in different tabs: with memory-only storage, each tab has its own personal session, so one tab can be signed in and the next not.
    - Desktop app and browser keep separate storage, so a person signed in on one is signed out on the other.
    - An Obsidian vault synced between people shares one `PlatformAccount`, so a claim from one device covers the content of everyone who shares the vault. The claim flow should warn about this.
  - Open: which touchpoints the first release needs. Cross-space search, the status indicator and connect/reconnect look like the minimum, because search is the first feature that depends on the personal session.

**The example.** Alice's Roam account has access in graphs A, B and C. Mallory is a member of A only, so she holds A's space password and can make claims as A. In the diagram, green means the claim gives access there, grey means it doesn't, and red means access gained by forgery.

**The difference in a sentence or two.** Under both options, a claim that is fully proven (attested) reaches every space where that platform account has access. The options differ on an unproven (asserted) claim. Option 1 gives it no access at all. Option 2 gives it access only in the space that vouched for it.

**Option 1: reach follows identity**
- 1a: Alice gets no access until she proves her identity (L1, L6 or L8). After that, she reaches A, B and C.
- 1b: This shows why proof has to come first. If an unproven claim were accepted, Mallory could claim Alice's uid while acting as A and reach B and C, graphs she was never in.
- Cost: cross-space search waits on the identity-link decision.

**Option 2: reach scoped by attestation**
- 2a: Alice connects from A without proof. Her claim reaches A only.
- 2b: She opens the plugin in B, so B vouches too. She now reaches A and B, but not C.
- 2c: Mallory forges a claim from A. It reaches only A, which she can already read with the password, so she gains nothing.
- 2d: Alice proves her identity. The same claim now reaches A, B and C, with no new kind of record.
- Cost: until she proves her identity, Alice connects each space once.
- Benefit: cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision.

- Mermaid stacks the graphs as C, A, B, not alphabetically. Fixing that would mean hand-placing nodes, so I left it.
- Option 2 is drawn higher than Option 1, though Option 1 is on the left.

- Glossary
  - **Space**: one Roam graph or Obsidian vault connected to Discourse Graphs.
  - **Pseudo-user**: a login (a row in `auth.users`) that stands for something other than a person: a space, a group, `everyone`, or an agent.
  - **Space password, space session**: the shared credential stored in the platform settings. Every member of the graph can read it. Logging in with it means acting as the space, not as a person.
  - **Personal account, personal session**: a Discourse Graphs account for one person, and a login as that person. Neither exists yet.
  - **Platform account** (`PlatformAccount`): a person as a platform knows them. A Roam user has the same uid, so the same platform account, in every graph. An Obsidian platform account belongs to one vault.
  - **`LocalAccess`**: the record that a platform account takes part in a space.
  - **Co-member**: someone in the same space, who therefore holds the space password and can act as the space.
  - **Claim**: a personal account's statement "this platform account is me". It is stored on the platform account (`dg_account`).
  - **Vouching space**: the space whose session made the claim. Because that session is shared, it shows only that someone in that space made the claim, not who.
  - **Attestation level**: how well a claim is proven.
    - `asserted`: only vouched for by a space session. Any co-member could have made it.
    - `corroborated`: two or more spaces recorded the same platform account details before the claim (layer L2).
    - `attested`: proven by a check that a co-member can't fake, such as email binding (L1), a Roam backend token (L6) or a Roam sign-in token (L8).
    - `frozen`: a competing claim arrived, and the claim gives no access until it is settled (L3).
  - **Access claim, identity claim**: an access claim only lets the person act in the vouching space. An identity claim says who the person is everywhere, and so carries attribution. The difference is the attestation level, not a different record.
  - **Reach**: the spaces a person can act for through their claims.
  - **Lease**: a person's access through a space lasts while they keep using the plugin there (`LocalAccess.last_seen`). 90 days is a placeholder.
  - **Cap**: a limit on what a claim or a grant allows, for example read-only.
  - **Group**: a set of spaces that share content with each other. Each group has a pseudo-user.
  - **`everyone`**: the pseudo-user that public content is shared with. Every caller counts as `everyone`, logged in or not.
  - **Agent**: a pseudo-user for an AI agent. It reads what its one principal (a person or a space) reads, usually capped to read-only.

**What gets easier**
- **Layout:** I set every coordinate myself. Mermaid's ordering and Roam's old renderer stop mattering: a 2x2 grid is just four positions.
- **Titles:** frames are named regions, and tldraw draws the name above the frame, so nothing covers it.

- **Arrows:** plain arrows go between two fixed points and don't attach to boxes. If someone moves a box, its arrows stay behind and must be redrawn. Arrows that do stay attached exist only for discourse nodes with typed relations, which doesn't suit these diagrams.
